page: Microsoft Azure M416s_v2 is an ultra-high-capacity memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is driven by Intel Xeon 8280L processors with dedicated CPU allocation, offering 416 vCPUs derived from 208 physical cores at a 2.7 GHz base frequency. It incorporates 5,700 GB of system memory, yielding 13.7 GB per vCPU, and includes 8,796 GB of integrated local SSD storage without discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional parallel execution and memory throughput alongside modest single-core throughput. The M416s_v2 achieves top-decile scores in stress-ng multi-core testing, PassMark CPU tests, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, reaching 1,425.6 GB/sec. Memory subsystems demonstrate high throughput, exceeding 767 GB/sec in large uncached reads and driving 260.18 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Conversely, single-threaded metrics, including Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression, place in the bottom 25% of evaluated cloud servers.

From an architectural perspective, the M416s_v2 consolidates expansive multi-socket footprints into a single virtualized deployment, minimizing node sprawl for monolithic memory architectures. The primary tradeoff is the reliance on extensive parallelism; workloads bound by single-thread clock speed will encounter bottlenecks. Additionally, while prompt processing for 7B parameter language models shows competitive throughput, CPU-bound text generation speeds remain low.

The hardware configuration aligns directly with memory-bound enterprise systems. Primary workload fits include multi-terabyte in-memory database platforms such as SAP HANA, massive distributed caching layers, large-scale Redis architectures, and heavy analytical data processing tasks requiring immense local memory capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure M416s_v2 is a memory-optimized instance designed for hyper-scale database and high-concurrency workloads. Powered by Intel Xeon 8280L processors running at 2.7 GHz, it features 416 dedicated vCPUs across 208 physical cores, 5,700 GB of system memory, and 8,796 GB of bundled local SSD storage without discrete GPUs. The platform demonstrates top-tier multi-core execution and memory bandwidth in synthetic benchmarks, sustaining 260.18 million Redis SET operations per second and high multi-threaded decompression rates. However, single-core benchmarks such as Geekbench and single-threaded compression place in lower quartiles, reflecting an emphasis on horizontal scaling over raw per-core clock speed. Because of its massive aggregate capacity, the instance offers high consolidation density for large infrastructure footprints. The M416s_v2 is primarily suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis deployments, enterprise resource planning systems, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
